original_question: What is the generic name of the lightest carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (by molar mass) that has been used to treat certain cases of nystagmus and has been used to treat patients with normal pressure hydrocephalus in clinical trials?

final_qi.question: What is the generic name of the lightest carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (by molar mass) that has been used to treat certain cases of nystagmus and has been used to treat patients with normal pressure hydrocephalus in clinical trials?
final_qi.search_keyword: lightest carbonic anhydrase inhibitor nystagmus normal pressure hydrocephalus
final_qi.long_answer: The drug referred to is acetazolamide. It is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor that has been noted for its relatively low molar mass compared to other drugs in its class. Acetazolamide has been used in the treatment of certain cases of nystagmus and has also been applied in clinical trials for patients with normal pressure hydrocephalus, where its mechanism of action helps in managing the fluid dynamics within the brain.
